messages:
sam: Heads-up: seeing ~9% gpu-attach failures in eu-west3 since 04:02 UTC. provisioner shows nvme cmd timeouts and 'io-queue-full'.
tara: any infra-rollouts or network churn overnight?
ben: we rolled smaller scrub window changes at 03:40 and flipped preserve-flag auto-prune at 03:50.
storage-bot: cron-job started: 'ephemeral-scrub' at 03:55 UTC on cohort eu-west3-*. concurrency=6.
sam: here's top of iostat from node gw-eu-78:
```
Device       r/s     w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1      1.2  310.8    4.8 19840    63.8    12.4   45.6  0.12  96.7
```
ben: avgqu > 10 and %util ~97 — local writeback pile-up. but interestingly network egress errors spiked during same window.
tara: why would egress affect nvme? are we seeing objectstore retries backing up writeback?
ben: yes. services that flush temp checkpoints to S3 fallback on retries -> syncs block on local fsync causing long tail writes; combined with heavy scrub it saturates nvme queues.
sam: ops-bot shows egress-route flaps to us-west-eu backbone 03:48-04:05 UTC.
storage-bot: alert: 'egress.retry_rate' spiked x9 in eu-west3 at 03:49 UTC.
ben: mitigation plan: 1) pause ephemeral-scrub on eu-west3 (rolling stop), 2) set kernel vm.dirty_ratio=5 and vm.dirty_bytes=33554432 on affected hosts, 3) reduce janitor concurrency to 2, 4) route new gpu-provisions to eu-west1 for 45m (policy 'avoid:eu-west3').
tara: pls run the flag flip for janitor: `curl -XPOST https://flags.internal/flip -d '{"key":"janitor.max_writeback","value":"2","scope":"eu-west3"}'`
sam: paused scrub for 40% of hosts -> attach failures down from 9.2% -> 1.8% in 7m.
ben: added short-term alert: when nvme.avgqu > 8 AND provisioner.attach_errors > 5% fire page.
pager: incident opened: INC-2026-92. tagging storage, network, and release. please push host list and stack traces to the incident doc.
tara: followups: audit objectstore client retry configs, add network-aware throttling for scrub, stage a load test that combines objectstore retries and janitor to catch this early.
ben: filing ticket STORAGE-489 with timeline, host dumps, proposed kernel tunables, and test plan.
sam: looping legal for any customer-impacted SLA items. :eyes:
pager: acknowledged and paging oncall-sre and network-team. :rotating_light:
